title: La-Z-Boy Canada Lineup Analysis
fit_evidence_note: This evidence incorporates the user's Canadian La-Z-Boy Recliner Research document. Its claims remain attributed secondary evidence unless it cites a readable primary Canadian manufacturer source. Manufacturer US tear-pad dimensions are market/configuration specific. Never convert chair shipping weight into user capacity; disputed fit claims are withheld from recommendations.
source_note: This reference combines the user's Canadian La-Z-Boy Recliner Research and earlier web research. Dealer-provided fit guidance is secondary evidence, not a manufacturer-confirmed anthropometric recommendation. Dimensions are specific to their cited market and configuration. The uploaded research's Pinnacle 350-lb capacity applies to the 1PL512 Platinum lift configuration only; do not infer it for the regular recliner. All other missing capacities remain unknown. Conflicting models are withheld from candidate lists.
coverage_note: The source calls itself a lineup analysis but does not establish a complete, current Canadian SKU catalog. Validate active Canadian models and options against current Canadian tear pads or official dealer materials.

fit_claim.statement: A La-Z-Boy Canada dealer article describes Pinnacle as small-scale for people 5′4″ to 5′9″.
Described as petite / smaller-frame seating; no numeric user-height range found.
Dealer product listings describe James as tall scale (5′10″ to 6′2″), contradicting its placement in the supplied Canada analysis small/medium band.
Dealer product listings describe Rowan as small scale (5′4″ to 5′9″).
Canadian retailer lists Harbor Town as small scale (5′4″ to 5′9″).

Canadian La-Z-Boy dealer calls Trouper a top seller for shorter customers, while US dealer listings describe its rocking recliner as tall scale (5′10″ to 6′2″). The sectional tear pad does not include fit dimensions.
Dealer product listing describes Morrison as tall scale (5′10″ to 6′2″).
Dealer product listing describes Greyson as tall scale (5′10″ to 6′2″).
Dealer listings describe Astor as extra-tall scale (6′3″ and up); official US product copy describes a deep, wide seat and a tall base.

Official US product copy says Redwood is designed especially for taller users; La-Z-Boy Vancouver dealer describes it as designed for larger, heavier people, without a numeric user-height or weight capacity.
Dealer product listing describes Randell as tall scale (5′10″ to 6′2″); official La-Z-Boy specification details were not confirmed in this research.
Dealer product listings describe Ace as extra-tall scale (6′3″ and up); official US product copy describes it as extra-large scale.

entries.title: Canadian dealer pricing and surcharges (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis claims Canadian orders use Canadian-dollar transactions based on U.S.-dollar wholesale lists and that some lines may have import surcharges. It supplies no current exchange rate, surcharge schedule, dealer terms, or calculation method. Do not calculate or quote prices from this claim.

entries.title: Motion-cycle testing (source claim)
entries.claim: The document claims manual and power recline assemblies are tested for 100,000 cycles under a 300 lb load per seat; headrest and lumbar mechanisms for 7,500 articulations; and rocker springs for 500,000 oscillations. These figures have not been independently verified and should not be presented as a warranty or lifespan promise.

entries.title: Frame construction (source claim)
entries.claim: The document describes a four-sided wood-and-steel unibody chassis and a proprietary OSB panel, with comparative strength and moisture-resistance percentages. The engineering composition and numerical comparisons require manufacturer confirmation.

entries.title: Reclina-Rocker mechanism (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis associates prefix 010 with a manual rocker recliner and describes independent back recline, a 16-position ratcheting arc, a three-position legrest, and under-seat tension adjusters. Verify prefix function and feature availability by model.

entries.title: Reclina-Way wall recliner mechanism (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis associates prefix 016 with a track-and-wheel wall recliner and claims as little as 5 inches of clearance. The existing local catalog currently describes 016 as a glider recliner, so this conflict must be resolved against a current source before use.

entries.title: Reclina-Glider mechanism (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis associates prefix 017 with a manual glider, 360-degree swivel, independent back recline, and one-position legrest. Verify the swivel and operation details for each model.

entries.title: Power recline platform P10/P16 (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis describes two motors for back and leg movement and a four-button control with USB. Verify motor count and controls by current model-specific documentation.

entries.title: Power headrest platform (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis describes three motors for back, leg, and headrest movement, a headrest articulation angle up to 55 degrees, toggle controls, home button, and USB. Treat as a general claim needing model-specific confirmation.

entries.title: Power headrest and lumbar platform (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis describes four motors and lumbar extension up to 3 inches, in addition to back, leg, and headrest movement. Verify exact prefix meanings and model compatibility.

entries.title: Wireless remote upgrade (source claim)
entries.claim: The source claims compatible multi-actuator remotes provide two memory presets, auto-home, a locator, magnetic cradle, and a control lock. Model and option compatibility are not established.

entries.title: Power mechanism obstruction safety (source claim)
entries.claim: The document claims a spring-loaded disengagement system protects motors when a closing mechanism encounters an obstruction. Do not treat this as a safety guarantee without manufacturer confirmation.

entries.title: Petite fit band (research suggestion)
entries.claim: The analysis suggests a height band of 5 ft 4 in and under, with seat depth 18–19.5 in and seat height 18–19 in, and mentions Pinnacle 512 and Vail 403. It does not provide model-specific supporting dimensions or Canadian verification; do not use as an automatic recommendation.

entries.title: Small-to-medium fit band (research suggestion)
entries.claim: The analysis suggests 5 ft 5 in–5 ft 9 in, seat depth 19.5–20.5 in, and seat height 19–20 in; it names James 521, Rowan 765, and Harbor Town 799. Verify model dimensions and source before recommending.

entries.title: Tall/large fit band (research suggestion)
entries.claim: The analysis suggests 5 ft 10 in–6 ft 2 in, seat depth 20.5–22 in, and seat height 20–21 in; it names Trouper 724, Morrison 766, and Greyson 530. Verify each model's dimensions; this is not medical or guaranteed-fit advice.

entries.title: Extra-tall fit band (research suggestion)
entries.claim: The analysis suggests 6 ft 3 in and taller, seat depth 21–23 in, and seat height 21–22.5 in; it names Astor 519 and Summit models. The document does not substantiate dimensions by model; do not use as an automatic recommendation.

entries.title: Summit Series models and construction (source claim)
entries.claim: The source groups Redwood 776, Randell 777, and Ace 805 as Summit Series and claims a taller solid-wood base, wider chassis, five springs per seat, reinforced drive rods, 2.5 lb foam, and additional calf support. Confirm exact model membership, specifications, and availability with current Canadian literature.

entries.title: Bronze lift tier (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis lists Liam 786, Jean 793, and Billie 794 at 300 lb, with a sequential one-motor lift/recline system and 13-inch clearance. Verify per-model rating and clearance before use.

entries.title: Silver lift tier (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis lists James 521 at 325 lb, with two motors and 5-inch clearance. Confirm against current model tear pads and Canadian warranty/spec sheets.

entries.title: Gold lift tier (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis lists Clayton 562 at 500 lb and claims three motors, 13-inch clearance, six massage motors, and warming pads. Verify every specification and current availability.

entries.title: Platinum lift tier (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis lists Pinnacle 512 and Astor 519 at 350 lb, with 1PL/1PH configurations, enclosed bases, 12-inch clearance, and zero-gravity positioning. Verify by exact model and prefix before use.

entries.title: Recliner prefix taxonomy (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis groups 010/P10, 10U/10X, 016/P16/16X, 017, and lift prefixes 1HM, 1PL/1PH, 4LP/3BL by mechanism. Prefix aliases and motor/feature meanings may vary by model; confirm with tear pads.

entries.title: La-Z-Time 400-series prefix taxonomy (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis describes sofa, loveseat, console loveseat, drop-down table sofa, and chair-and-a-half families, plus left/right modular pieces and power/headrest/lumbar variants. Mid-run-only notes appear for some modular prefixes. Verify exact combinations and model-run applicability.

entries.title: Reclina-Way 300-series prefix taxonomy (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis groups wall sofa, loveseat, and console loveseat prefixes with power/headrest/lumbar variants. Confirm nomenclature and hardware availability by model.

entries.title: Stationary, sleeper, accent, and duo prefixes (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis lists these family/code groupings: 510/520/555 sleeper frames; 610/620/630 stationary frames; 230/240/855 accent/ottoman/chair-and-a-half; 061/063/023 Comfort Essentials; and P91/P93/P94 duo. Verify names and active Canadian applicability.

entries.title: Cushion core density and application claims
entries.claim: The source describes standard, Ultra Plush, ComfortCore Premier, FS Contour, Z6, and DC cushion systems, with foam density/layering claims and suggested applications. The text contains questionable unit notation (for example, foam density rendered as '27 lb/cu. ft. (1.8 Density)'); do not copy numerical density values into product specs until the original engineering source clarifies units.

entries.title: Bucket seat geometry (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis distinguishes Original, Sculpted, and Hybrid bucket geometries and claims different side-wedge densities, including 440/444 variants. Verify exact model and production-run applicability.

entries.title: Wearability classes and motion restrictions (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis says Normal/Black Dot is broadly approved, Medium/Green Dot is limited to stationary, sleeper, duo, high-leg, and occasional-chair frames, and Performance/P Dot is broadly approved. It explicitly prohibits Medium on motion prefixes. These are high-impact buildability rules; do not enforce them until checked against official current CAP/cover documents.

entries.title: i-Clean stain coverage (source claim)
entries.claim: The document lists example covered and excluded stains and claims a three-year stain warranty. This is not the warranty text; refer customers to current written Canadian warranty and care instructions.

entries.title: Specialty fabric treatment terms (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis describes Pet Friendly (PF), Conserve (c), Antimicrobial (A), Restore by Nanobionic (N), and Bleach Cleanable (WB/W*B) treatments. Availability and marketing claims are not verified for the Canadian market or for any specific cover.

entries.title: CAP codes and cutting/orientation (source claim)
entries.claim: The source describes UR, DR, VS, PS, DP, NP, UE, BU, and RL cutting/orientation or venting implications. Local CAP catalog definitions may differ; do not change SKU logic or selection rules based on this summary alone.

entries.title: Leather classifications and treatment claims
entries.claim: The source distinguishes Authentic, Performance, Nubuck, Crypton, and iClean leather and describes surface treatments and care properties. It cites examples such as Athena FL1932, but these are not confirmed active Canadian offerings.

entries.title: Leather application tiers and pillow restriction (source claim)
entries.claim: The document describes SLR/SLS/CLM/CLP leather application tiers and claims P1 accent pillows cannot use LL/LS/LM/RL/BU/UE covers, requiring a separate valid fabric or omission of pillows. Treat as a critical candidate validation rule pending confirmation from the cited leather and CAP documents.

entries.title: Battery SKUs, run-time, and compatibility (source claim)
entries.claim: The analysis names 088BP1 single and 088BP2 dual packs, claims 5–7 hours charging and 5–7 days operation at ten cycles per day, and lists prefix compatibility. It excludes lift chairs, power-console bundles, and drop-down tables. Existing app codes use BP1/BP2; the 088 SKU crosswalk is not verified. Do not generate or reject orders from these claims yet.

entries.title: Power console bundles (source claim)
entries.claim: The source lists CB/CC/CM finishes, selected console loveseat and modular prefixes, outlets, USB, wireless charging, and accessory SKUs. Verify voltage, components, eligible models, and Canadian electrical specifications before customer-facing use.

entries.title: Drop-down table and swivel/base options (source claim)
entries.claim: The document describes 446/U46/X46 table features and power requirements, SL/SW swivel options, tall-base kits, and handle options. Exact fit, prefix, and SKU compatibility is not established; verify against model-specific tear pads.

entries.title: Warranty matrix (source claim; not Canadian warranty text)
entries.claim: The analysis claims limited lifetime for manual mechanisms/frames/springs, five years for duo mechanisms, three years for power motors/electronics and certain iClean stains, and one year for batteries, foam, and standard fabric/leather seam or nap loss. This conflicts with existing local warranty summaries and is not a substitute for the current Canadian written warranty.

entries.title: Five proposed validation stages
entries.claim: The analysis proposes: ergonomic/capacity filtering; mechanical prefix selection; fabric wearability validation; leather tier and accent-pillow checks; and battery/electronics compatibility. This is a candidate validation checklist only; no rules are enabled until their source data and model-specific exceptions are verified.

entries.title: Citations and document extraction caveats
entries.claim: The analysis cites several separate PDFs and web pages, but their contents are not all attached with this resource. The extracted document contains malformed table separators and stray 'h>' text. Treat quoted tables as leads; verify original source pages and dates before importing specifications or rules.
